title: Piety as beginning and end of the virtues
english: Piety must be cultivated above all things. It is rightly called the mother of the virtues, for it is the beginning and end of the virtues. Both sight and the natural law teach us to know God, the sustaining and creating cause of all things: sight, as it falls upon visible and firmly established things; the natural law, as through those same visible and ordered things it reasons out their author.
translator_notes: True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify.
orientation: The work opens with a maxim on piety, then explains how knowledge of God as the sustaining and creating cause of all things is taught by sight and by the natural law.
